# Banner

Figma: [05c. Banner](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-924) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-07

Full-width contextual notification, larger and more prominent than Alert. 30 variants encode 5 tones × 3 styles × 2 directions. 40px tinted icon circle on the leading edge, title/description/optional link stacked, optional primary action button as a solid tone-colored pill, dismiss control on the trailing edge. Use for page-level announcements, system-wide messages, account-level warnings, and marketing/upsell calls-to-action. NEW in Syntropy v2.0 (no direct legacy counterpart). Related to but distinct from Alert (inline status), Toast (transient notifications), and Hero/CardAction patterns.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/banner/reference.png`

### Banner

Large page-level notification with icon circle, title, description, optional link, solid action pill and close, in Filled, Outlined or Elevated style. One per screen; also the preferred mobile RTL alert surface.

Level: molecule

Use when:
- KYC or IBAN verification reminder at the top of home with a Verify action
- Scheduled maintenance notice (showClose=false)
- Account-level failure such as payout transfer failed with Retry
- Feature announcement or upsell with a CTA (Style=Elevated)

Don't use when:
- Inline message inside a form or card: use Alert
- Transient confirmation: use Toast
- Required decision: use Dialog
- Permanent compliance disclosure on a deal: use ShariaDisclosure
- Two or more banners on one screen: keep one, demote the rest to Alert or Toast

Accessibility: role=status (role=alert for error); keep close available except for system-critical messages; Show Title can hide the title for body-only banners.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Banner is the page-level notification primitive. Larger and more prominent than Alert, Banner is meant to be the most attention-grabbing message on the screen. Use it for system-wide announcements, account-level warnings, marketing/upsell calls-to-action, and any contextual message that warrants a primary action button. Three styles encode the visual treatment: Filled (high attention), Outlined (medium attention), Elevated (floating page-top placement).

### When to reach for Banner

- Page-top system announcements ("Scheduled maintenance Sunday 02:00 - 04:00").
- Account-level warnings that need a clear action ("Your CMA license expires in 30 days - Renew").
- Marketing or upsell messages with a CTA ("Upgrade to premium for early access - Try free").
- Onboarding nudges that introduce a feature or capability ("Complete your profile to unlock premium deals").
- KYC or compliance reminders that occupy a dedicated row at the top of the page.

### When NOT to use Banner

- Inline form-field errors or validation messages - use Alert.
- Brief transient confirmations that auto-dismiss - use Toast.
- Full-screen blocking confirmations - use Modal/Dialog.
- Persistent status next to a single field - use FieldHelper.
- Multiple competing Banners on one page - pick the most important one. A Banner that is one of three is no longer a Banner.

### Sample tones

### Anatomy

A Banner has up to five elements arranged horizontally. From the leading edge to the trailing edge in LTR: icon circle, title with optional description and link, primary action button, close X. RTL mirrors visually but the data model is the same.

### Elements

- Icon circle: 40px circular container with a tinted background (matches the tone) holding the 24px tone icon. Defaults vary per tone (info → Icon/info, success → Icon/check, warning → Icon/alert-triangle, error → Icon/dangerous, neutral → Icon/info). Swap via Figma's nested instance UI when you need a custom icon.
- Title (title TEXT): bold 16px tone-colored. The most important piece of content. Always present. Keep it scannable.
- Description (description TEXT, controlled by showDescription BOOLEAN): regular 13px muted. One to two sentences of context. Default ON. Hide for title-only banners.
- Link (linkText TEXT, controlled by showLink BOOLEAN): semibold 13px tone-colored inline link. Default OFF. Use for "Read more" / "Learn how" pointing to docs.
- Button (buttonLabel TEXT, controlled by showButton BOOLEAN): solid tone-colored pill chip with white text. Default OFF. Use for the primary action ("Renew", "Verify", "Upgrade"). Keep label short (one or two words).
- Close icon (closeIcon INSTANCE_SWAP, default Icon/x): tap-to-dismiss control. Hide via showClose=false for non-dismissible banners (e.g. system maintenance warnings that must persist).

### Tones

Five tones convey semantic meaning. Pick the tone based on what the banner MEANS, not what looks nice.

Tone = info

Default. Use for neutral announcements ("New deals available", "Feature launched"). The blue says "here is something useful".

Tone = success

Use for high-impact confirmation ("KYC approved", "Account upgraded"). The green says "this is good news worth surfacing prominently".

Tone = warning

Use for issues that need attention but are not yet blocking ("License expires soon", "Profile incomplete"). The amber says "please look at this".

Tone = error

Use for failures or account-level issues ("Payment failed", "Verification rejected"). The red says "this is broken and needs your attention". Reserve for true errors.

Tone = neutral

Use for low-priority announcements that should not dominate visually ("Scheduled maintenance", "Help center now open"). The gray says "FYI, not urgent".

### Styles

Three styles encode the visual treatment. Same tone, different presence. Pick by how loud the banner should feel relative to the surrounding content.

Style = Filled

Tinted background + tone border. Highest visual weight. The icon circle is transparent (blends with the bg). Use for the most prominent system-wide announcements that need to dominate the visual hierarchy.

Style = Outlined

White (bg/surface) background + tone border + tinted icon circle. Medium visual weight. The icon circle has its own tinted bg to give it presence against the white background. Use when the banner sits inside a tinted page or card where Filled would clash.

Style = Elevated

bg/elevated background + drop shadow + tinted icon circle, no border. Suggests the banner floats above the content. Use for page-top placement where the banner reads as a floating layer rather than embedded content. Also good for marketing/upsell banners where the shadow adds visual interest.

### In context - common patterns

Four Safqah Banner patterns showing real usage.

### Pattern 1: Page-top system announcement

Scheduled maintenance window appears as a non-dismissible neutral Banner at the top of every authenticated page. Visible until the maintenance is complete. Filled style for clear visual presence; showClose=false because the user cannot dismiss a system-level warning.

### Pattern 2: Marketing/upsell with primary CTA

Upsell to a premium tier or a new feature uses Elevated style for the floating "marketing layer" feel. Includes the primary CTA button. Dismissible (the user has seen it and can move on).

### Pattern 3: KYC reminder with link

Account-level reminder pointing to a help center article. Use warning tone for the "please take action" feel, Outlined style to coexist with a tinted card layout. showLink=true to expose the inline link to documentation.

### Pattern 4: Account-level error with retry

When payment processing fails at the account level (not field-specific), use an error Banner with a button to retry. Filled style for maximum visibility. The button takes the user directly to the retry flow.

### Properties guide

Banner exposes 9 properties: 4 TEXT for content, 4 BOOLEAN for visibility, 1 INSTANCE_SWAP for the close icon. The tone icon (info/check/triangle/etc) is not exposed as a named property - it varies per-variant by design and can be customized via Figma's nested instance UI.

### TEXT properties

title  ·  TEXT

Default: "Banner title"

The bold tone-colored title. Always present. Keep it scannable - one short sentence. Avoid generic openings like "Notice:" or "Attention:".

description  ·  TEXT

Default: "Descriptive supporting text explaining what this banner is about."

One to two sentences of supporting context. Hide via showDescription=false for title-only banners.

linkText  ·  TEXT

Default: "Learn more"

Short inline link CTA. Use phrases like "Read more", "Learn how", "View settings". Only visible when showLink=true.

buttonLabel  ·  TEXT

Default: "Take action"

Primary action button label. Use one or two words - verbs like "Renew", "Verify", "Upgrade", "Retry". Only visible when showButton=true.

### BOOLEAN properties

showDescription  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the description visibility. Hide for title-only banners.

showLink  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: false

Toggle the inline link. Use for contextual pointers to docs or settings.

showButton  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: false

Toggle the primary CTA button. Use ONLY when the banner has a clear primary action - a banner with no clear action should not have a button.

showClose  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the close X icon. Hide for non-dismissible banners (system maintenance, blocking warnings, compliance reminders).

### INSTANCE_SWAP properties

closeIcon  ·  INSTANCE_SWAP

Default: Icon/x

The dismiss control icon. Almost always Icon/x.

> **Info:** There is NO named property for the tone icon. The tone icon is set per-variant inside the component (info icon for info, check for success, etc.) and varies automatically when the designer changes the Tone variant. To customize the tone icon, drill into the nested instance and use Figma's "Swap instance" UI. Same pattern as Alert and Toast.

### Code examples - Flutter

### Basic usage

```dart
// System maintenance announcement
const SyntropyBanner(
  tone: BannerTone.neutral,
  style: BannerStyle.filled,
  title: 'Scheduled maintenance - Sunday 02:00 to 04:00 KSA',
  description: 'Safqah will be unavailable during this window.',
  showClose: false,
)

// Marketing/upsell with primary CTA
SyntropyBanner(
  tone: BannerTone.info,
  style: BannerStyle.elevated,
  title: 'New premium tier is live',
  description: 'Get early access to top-tier deals and lower fees.',
  showButton: true,
  buttonLabel: 'Upgrade',
  onButtonTap: () => Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/upgrade'),
  onClose: () => prefs.setBool('upgrade_banner_dismissed', true),
)

// Warning with link to docs
SyntropyBanner(
  tone: BannerTone.warning,
  style: BannerStyle.outlined,
  title: 'Verify your identity to access premium deals',
  description: 'Upload your national ID to unlock the full catalog.',
  showLink: true,
  linkText: 'Read the KYC guide',
  onLinkTap: () => launchUrl(Uri.parse('https://safqah.sa/help/kyc')),
)

// Arabic RTL banner
SyntropyBanner(
  tone: BannerTone.warning,
  style: BannerStyle.filled,
  direction: TextDirection.rtl,
  title: 'تنتهي صلاحية ترخيص هيئة السوق المالية خلال 30 يومًا',
  description: 'جدد الآن للحفاظ على الوصول إلى الصفقات المميزة.',
  showButton: true,
  buttonLabel: 'تجديد',
)
```

### Implementation sketch

```dart
enum BannerTone { info, success, warning, error, neutral }
enum BannerStyle { filled, outlined, elevated }

class SyntropyBanner extends StatelessWidget {
  final String title;
  final String? description;
  final String? linkText;
  final String? buttonLabel;
  final BannerTone tone;
  final BannerStyle style;
  final TextDirection direction;
  final bool showClose;
  final VoidCallback? onClose;
  final VoidCallback? onLinkTap;
  final VoidCallback? onButtonTap;

  const SyntropyBanner({
    super.key,
    required this.title,
    this.description,
    this.linkText,
    this.buttonLabel,
    this.tone = BannerTone.info,
    this.style = BannerStyle.filled,
    this.direction = TextDirection.ltr,
    this.showClose = true,
    this.onClose,
    this.onLinkTap,
    this.onButtonTap,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final tokens = _tokensFor(tone, theme);
    
    return Directionality(
      textDirection: direction,
      child: Container(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(20),
        decoration: _decorationFor(style, tokens, theme),
        child: Row(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            // Icon circle (40px)
            Container(
              width: 40, height: 40,
              decoration: BoxDecoration(
                color: style == BannerStyle.filled ? Colors.transparent : tokens.bgSubtle,
                shape: BoxShape.circle,
              ),
              alignment: Alignment.center,
              child: Icon(tokens.icon, color: tokens.iconColor, size: 24),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: 16),
            // Message block
            Expanded(child: Column(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
              children: [
                Text(title, style: theme.text.semibold16.copyWith(color: tokens.text)),
                if (description != null) ...[
                  const SizedBox(height: 6),
                  Text(description!, style: theme.text.regular13.copyWith(color: theme.text.muted)),
                ],
                if (linkText != null) ...[
                  const SizedBox(height: 6),
                  GestureDetector(
                    onTap: onLinkTap,
                    child: Text(linkText!, style: theme.text.semibold13.copyWith(color: tokens.text)),
                  ),
                ],
              ],
            )),
            // Action button
            if (buttonLabel != null) ...[
              const SizedBox(width: 16),
              _PillButton(label: buttonLabel!, color: tokens.text, onTap: onButtonTap),
            ],
            // Close
            if (showClose) ...[
              const SizedBox(width: 16),
              IconButton(
                icon: const Icon(SyntropyIcons.x, size: 16),
                onPressed: onClose,
              ),
            ],
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Warning:** There is no named INSTANCE_SWAP property for the tone icon. Binding such a property would force a single default icon across all 30 variants and erase the per-tone defaults. Designers swap the tone icon via Figma's "Swap instance" UI on the nested instance. Same trade-off applied to Alert and Toast.

> **Warning:** TEXT property defaults are English. RTL variants in the SET preview also show English because of a Figma constraint. Designers override per-instance with Arabic when placing an RTL variant. The reference frame demonstrates this correctly.

> **Info:** Banner is intentionally larger than Alert (560px wide vs ~400px, 20px padding vs 12px, 16px title vs 14px, 40px icon circle vs 20px icon). The size differences are functional, not arbitrary - Banner needs to dominate the visual hierarchy, Alert needs to sit calmly inside content.

> **Info:** The button is a SOLID tone-colored pill chip with white text, intentionally different from a typical Button/Primary because it sits inside a tinted Banner background. Do not replace it with a generic Button instance - the contrast tokens are specifically tuned for this context.

> **Warning:** When to use the close icon: keep showClose=true for most banners (let the user dismiss). Hide showClose=false ONLY for system-critical messages that must persist (scheduled maintenance, compliance violations, blocked accounts). Accessibility: do not hide the close icon casually.

> **Warning:** Multiple Banners on one page is a code smell. If you find a screen with 2+ Banners, ask: which is the most important? The other(s) probably belong as Alert (inline) or Toast (transient). A page with three Banners shouting at the user has effectively zero Banners.

> **Info:** The icon circle's tinted background is INTENTIONALLY only visible in Outlined and Elevated styles. In Filled style, the icon circle is transparent because adding a tinted bg on top of an already-tinted Banner bg would create visual noise. This is by design - do not "fix" it by adding a circle bg in Filled.

> **Tip:** Banner width is fixed at 560px. For wider page layouts, place the Banner in a constrained container or use a custom full-bleed wrapper. Do not stretch Banner beyond 560px - the layout proportions (icon : message : button : close) are tuned for this width.
